To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) low levels of tritium can induce genotoxic effects in the haemocyte cells of adult mussels; and (b) the bioconcentration of tritium in different tissues of the mussels is tissue-dependent and dose-related.

low doses of HTO (12-485 muGy h(-1)) induced significant genetic damage in the form of MN and single-strand DNA damage in the haematocytes of M. edulis, and that the tissue-specific bioconcentrating capacity of HTO in this species is different from that of the reference genotoxic agent (EMS) and other radionuclids.

(a) low concentrations of tritium are capable of inducing DNA damage in the haematopoietic tissue of the marine bivalve, Mytilus; and (b) tritium accumulates differentially in the tissues of this bivalve.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and validation of sensitive and relevant genotoxic assays for aquatic species and the use of these assays to assess the impact of environmentally-relevant radionuclide discharges on aquatic biota.
the development of new and innovative approaches to the study of the impact of low doses of radioactive substances on aquatic organisms.
establishing an integrated approach to the assessment of the impact of low-level tritium contamination in aquatic ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

tritium is a genotoxic agent and can bioconcentrate differentially in aquatic organisms, and that these effects need to be considered when assessing the impact of radionuclide discharges on the aquatic ecosystem.
the dose-response relationship is not a linear one, and the dose limits recommended by international bodies are not appropriate for the protection of all organisms.

the dose rate of 485 muGy/h is the highest dose rate that can be applied in a laboratory study to the adult life stage without inducing genotoxic effects in the haemocyte cells of M. edulis, and this is equivalent to a dose rate of 0.48 muGy/h.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tritium is capable of inducing genetic effects in marine mussels, and that the dose-response relationship is non-linear.
tritium is capable of causing genetic damage to the haemocytes in mussels at environmentally relevant concentrations and also bioaccumulates in a tissue-specific manner.
the dose rates of 12, 24 and 48 muGyh(- 1) were capable of inducing genotoxic effects in mussel haemocytes, but the dose of 6 muGyh(-) was not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current generic dose limits recommended for protection of aquatic biotas might be too conservative for some aquatic organisms.
, despite the very low concentrations of HTO used, we observed significant genotoxic effects and bioconcentration in the mussel.

, in addition to the need to develop and implement a rational framework to protect aquatic biota from radionuclide contamination, the need for a more comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms of radionuclide toxicity in aquatic biota is also imperative.
